title: Kohli Is Out With a Hamstring Injury. For the First Time in a Decade, India's No. 3 Spot Is Genuinely Open.
excerpt: Yashasvi Jaiswal replaces the injured Virat Kohli for the Afghanistan ODI series. The debate over who bats at No. 3 has only just begun.
body:
Virat Kohli will not be part of India's squad for the three-match ODI series against Afghanistan. The 37-year-old suffered a hamstring injury during Royal Challengers Bengaluru's IPL 2026 title run and has been advised rest for multiple weeks. In his place, the selectors have called up Yashasvi Jaiswal — a decision that has ignited debate about India's No. 3 position heading into the 2027 World Cup.

The ODI series begins on June 13 in Dharamsala. India have not played a 50-over match since January 2026, when they lost a bilateral series 1-2. With the ODI World Cup in South Africa just over a year away, every selection choice carries weight.

Why Jaiswal, Not Gaikwad

The choice of Jaiswal over Ruturaj Gaikwad — who scored a century at No. 4 for India A in the ongoing tri-series in Dambulla — was not accidental. Former India opener Aakash Chopra, speaking on his YouTube channel, explained the logic.

"Neither he nor Yashasvi Jaiswal has a chance of playing in the XI, unless Rohit Sharma isn't fully fit," Chopra said. "Rutu's number will also come at some stage, but he is auditioning for a middle-order role. He had scored a hundred when he was given a chance at that number. So that is where the opening should come."

The distinction is positional. Gaikwad is being groomed for the middle order; Jaiswal is being auditioned at the top. If Rohit Sharma is fully fit and opens alongside Shubman Gill, Jaiswal slots in at No. 3 — Kohli's spot.

The No. 3 Question

Former India assistant coach Abhishek Nayar backed Jaiswal for the No. 3 role on Star Sports. "Open with Shubman Gill and Rohit Sharma. Yashasvi Jaiswal will play at No. 3, Shreyas Iyer at No. 4, KL Rahul at No. 5, Hardik Pandya at No. 6," Nayar said — though Pandya has since been ruled out with a quadriceps strain.

Jaiswal's ODI numbers are limited but promising. In four matches, the left-hander has scored 171 runs at an average of 57, including a century against South Africa in 2025 when he replaced an injured Gill. His ability to bat with intent against both pace and spin makes him a natural fit for the first powerplay or the No. 3 slot.

The other wildcard is Ishan Kishan, who has not played an ODI for India in two years but was devastating in IPL 2026 — 602 runs in 15 matches. He could get a look-in later in the series.

The Injury Shadow

Kohli's absence adds to a growing list of concerns. Hardik Pandya, cleared by the BCCI Centre of Excellence on Tuesday, was ruled out on Wednesday after picking up a fresh quadriceps strain — reportedly during a bowling assessment at the CoE itself. The BCCI source confirmed a three-week recovery timeline.

Captain Rohit Sharma has been cleared and trained in Mohali on Wednesday. Both teams will depart for Dharamsala on Thursday. But the 39-year-old's hamstring injury during IPL 2026, which cost him several matches, remains a background worry.

What the Diaspora Should Watch

For the NRI cricket fan, this series is a window into India's 2027 World Cup planning. The No. 3 spot — Kohli's for over a decade — is now genuinely open. Whether Jaiswal seizes it, or the role eventually goes to Gaikwad, or even Ishan Kishan forces his way in, depends on what happens in Dharamsala, Lucknow, and Chennai over the next ten days.

Kohli's hamstring will heal. The more interesting question is whether India's ODI batting order can evolve past his shadow.
